answer: Sybil resistance rests on quadratic stake bonding: an agent's voting weight is the square root of the bond it locks, and each identity needs a unique, non-transferable commitment. A hollow account with no stake carries no weight, so minting thousands changes nothing. Real influence costs real capital: to double its say an attacker must lock four times the bond, and splitting one budget across a karst of fake wallets is caught by the shared nullifier. Climbing the influence spiral therefore burns slashable collateral at every turn, making the attack dearer than honest work.
